note.headline: We hear email is only being read by AI agents.
body: So I wrote you a card instead.

I'm Brian, and I work with brand and creative teams at Frontify. After reading what Atlassian has shared this year, a few ideas stuck with me. They're guesses, not conclusions. You know your world better than I do.
If one of them is interesting, I'd love to compare notes.
note.emailLine: You're seeing this from my email. It's the same page I left on a card at your San Francisco office.

hero.sub: Anyone at {name} can make a launch post or image in seconds now. Without the brand's context, AI guesses: the wrong colors, the wrong voice and claims nobody approved.
hero.prompt: Make a LinkedIn post and image for our next Rovo launch.
hero.generic: Excited to announce an amazing new feature! Our innovative AI solution will revolutionize the way your team works. Don't miss out! #Innovation #AI #Teamwork
hero.onbrand: Rovo just learned a new trick. Ask it a question and it pulls the answer from work your team already did. No digging, no tab maze. Try it this week and tell us what it should learn next.

context.label: Tone of voice
context.value: Bold, optimistic, practical with a wink

hero.disclaimer: Illustrative draft written for this sample, using Atlassian's public brand personality guidance. Not Atlassian content.
hero.headline: AI is making everyone a creative.
hero.headline2: That doesn't mean they're good at it.
hero.badCaption: Looks fine at a glance. Look again: the generic headline, the posed thumbs-up, the wrong blue.
hero.badAlt: A fictional AI-generated LinkedIn graphic: a posed team giving thumbs-up, a teal gradient and a generic headline

check.title: Then it checks the work
check.sub: Before anything goes live, Brand Check reviews it against {name}'s guidelines, flags potential issues, and shows which guideline informed each finding.
check.note: Brand Check runs on the context you already keep in Frontify. It's more than a prompt: it's a service built into Frontify, available in the portal and through the API. The image is fictional AI-generated work content, and the findings are samples.

asset.by: fictional, made with a generic AI image tool
asset.alt: A fictional AI-generated LinkedIn graphic: a posed team giving thumbs-up, a teal gradient and a generic headline

findings.text: The teal-to-blue gradient overlay isn't in the brand palette.
findings.recommendation: Use Brand blue, #1868DB, on neutral backgrounds, with no color wash over photos.

findings.text: "Work Smarter Together With AI" is a generic AI claim, not approved Rovo messaging.
findings.recommendation: Start from the approved positioning, like "Less busywork. More teamwork."

findings.text: A posed group giving thumbs-up to the camera doesn't match the photography style.
findings.recommendation: Use a candid photo of a real team at work from the photo library.

contexts.eyebrow: Use case 2 · What context lives in Frontify
contexts.title: Every kind of context, in one place
contexts.sub: Brand, creative, product, event and partner guidance live in {name}'s portal, plus an Everyday section with short versions for every employee. People read them, and AI tools answer from them.
contexts.note: Sample pages built from Atlassian's public design system and product names. Not Atlassian's own guidelines.

items.label: Brand
items.title: Our palette
items.lead: Brand blue leads. Neutrals carry most of the page.
items.rule: Use Brand blue for primary actions and links only.
items.ask: What blue do I use for a button?
items.answer: Use **Brand blue, #1868DB**, for primary buttons and links.

items.label: Creative
items.title: Photography
items.lead: Real teams doing real work, never staged.

do.label: Teams at work
do.note: Candid moments of people working together.

dont.label: Posed for the camera
dont.note: No staged handshakes or stock smiles.

items.ask: Can I use a stock photo of a handshake?
items.answer: Better not. The photography guidelines ask for **candid teamwork**, and **no staged handshakes or stock smiles**.

items.label: Product

items.ask: Write a one-line pitch for Rovo.
items.answer: **Rovo is AI that works across the apps your team already uses, with the context of your work.** Drafted from the approved positioning.

items.label: Everyday
items.desc: Short rules for email, decks and docs
items.title: Email tone of voice
items.lead: The short version of our tone of voice, for everyone who sends email.
rules: Say what you need in under eight words.
Lead with the ask or the answer.
Use the standard signature. No quotes or images.
items.do: Can you review the launch plan by Thursday?
items.dont: Just circling back on the below!!
items.askLabel: Before sending, in Outlook with Copilot
items.ask: Check this email against our writing guidelines.
items.answer: Two fixes before you send: **put the ask in the first line**, and **use the standard signature**.
items.from: Condensed from Brand › Tone of voice

items.label: Partners
items.desc: What agencies and partners send, and how
items.title: Partner submission guide
items.lead: What agencies and marketplace partners need to know before they send work.
steps: Through Partners › Submit an asset in the portal, never by email.
Campaign, usage rights and an expiry date.
Approved logos, photos and templates in the portal.
items.rule: Every submission needs usage rights and an expiry date.
items.askLabel: A partner agency asks the brand assistant
items.ask: How do we send final files to the brand team?
items.answer: **Submit them in the portal** under Partners › Submit an asset, with **usage rights and an expiry date**. They land in the Partner submissions library.

everyday.eyebrow: Use case 4 · Everyday guidelines, inside your office applications
everyday.title: The right tone in every email and deck
everyday.sub: Most of {name} will never open a brand portal. With Frontify connected, Claude inside your email and presentation apps reads the Everyday guidelines and checks the work before it goes out.
everyday.note: Claude for Microsoft 365 reads Frontify through the Frontify connector (MCP) once it's set up in your Claude workspace. Sample email, deck and guidelines.

tabs.label: Email
tabs.ask: Check this email against our email tone of voice before I send it.
tabs.intro: Three fixes based on **Everyday › Email tone of voice**:

before.subject: Following up
body: Hi team, just circling back on the below!!
We've been heads-down on the Rovo launch and there's a lot going on, so I wanted to share where things stand.
Can you review the launch plan by Thursday?

after.subject: Review the Rovo launch plan by Thursday
body: Hi team, can you review the Rovo launch plan by Thursday?
It covers the messaging, launch assets and timeline. Comments in the doc are perfect.

fixes.label: Subject:
fixes.note: say what you need. "Following up" doesn't.

fixes.label: Opening:
fixes.note: lead with the ask. It's in the last line right now.

fixes.label: Sign-off:
fixes.note: use the standard signature, with no quotes.

tabs.done: Updated. The draft matches the email tone of voice and is ready to send.

tabs.label: Presentation
tabs.ask: Is this slide built the way our presentation guidelines say?

before.title: Q3 results and some thoughts on where we go next with the Rovo launch

fixes.label: Template:
fixes.note: this slide isn't on the company template.

fixes.label: Title:
fixes.note: 14 words. Keep titles to six or fewer.

fixes.label: Bullets:
fixes.note: six on one slide. Keep it to three.

tabs.done: Updated. Slide 2 now uses the company template and follows the presentation guidelines.

partners.eyebrow: Use case 5 · Partner and agency files
partners.title: Partner files land in the right place
partners.sub: Agencies and Marketplace partners submit work straight into {name}'s portal. Files land in the right library, and the assistant tags them and sets an expiry date in one sentence.
partners.note: Sample files, partner and library. The assistant acts on the assets you select: workflow status, metadata, tags and expiry dates.
partners.ask: Tag these Jira and Cleared for external use, and set them to expire Dec 31, 2026.
partners.plan: I'll add the tags Jira and Cleared for external use, and set Available until to Dec 31, 2026, on the 2 selected assets. Say yes and I'll apply it.
